subject: Request: Sylph9B entry exception & rollout questions
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 15 Jun 2028 08:23:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Sylph9B entry exception & rollout questions

Hi team,

Quick context: Sylph AI reached out with a new 9B variant (Sylph9B) that has promising latency/cost numbers in their benchmarks. Engineering has done a small compatibility sweep but there are two things that make me think this needs an exception to our usual version-lock process before we can schedule a normal intake:

- The variant uses a slightly different RoPE implementation and a custom tokenizer extension (adds two special tokens) — not a pure weights swap.
- Their recommended quantization strategy (4-bit mixed block) looks to conflict with our default KV-cache layout on some Ampere instances; we saw a 3–5ms increase in end-to-end token latency in local tests.

Attachments: sylph9b-variant-matrix.xlsx (compat notes from infra), sylph9b-ops-runbook.md (Sylph AI proposed runbook).

Ask: I want to request a scoped "entry exception" so we can run a weekend canary on a small dedicated pool and collect production telemetry (latency, token error rates, regen rate). Key questions:

1) Karthik — do we have a short checklist for tokenization-surface compatibility (edge cases like the extra tokens + streaming boundaries)? If so, can you confirm which tests are must-have before approving a canary?
2) Laura — product: if we go ahead with a canary, do we want feature gating (config flag) exposed to customers or keep it internal-only for the first 72 hours?
3) Marissa — ops: what capacity can we spare this weekend for a low-traffic canary (target ~50 rps peak)?

I recommend limiting the initial rollout to dedicated-us-central and pinning the model variant to prevent automatic rollforward while we evaluate. I realize this is a deviation from the normal intake; hence asking the group for a brief cross-functional sign-off.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick sync.

—Aditya
Aditya Rao
Head of Product Operations, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com


From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Cc: emily.jones@sylph.ai
Date: Fri, 15 Jun 2028 10:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Sylph9B entry exception & rollout questions

Thanks Aditya — good summary. A few quick product notes:

- We should treat this as an "internal-only" canary for the first 72 hours. We want to gather metrics and have an easy rollback path before any customer-facing exposure.
- Please add a short evaluation checklist in the runbook for quality regressions: (a) top-20 prompts from our existing regression suite, (b) sampling entropy comparison on generation endpoints, (c) regression-triggered alert thresholds (e.g., >3% unexpected shortenings or hallucination flags).

Karthik, can you list the KV/tokenizer tests Aditya mentioned? If we can get a pass/fail matrix by EOD today I can approve the scoped exception.

Also, Marissa — note we want a healthcheck that kills the canary automatically if token latency p95 exceeds the baseline by >30% for 10 minutes.

Laura
Laura Bennett

Hi all — thanks for the quick look. A couple clarifications from Sylph:

- The tokenizer extension is backward-compatible; the two extra tokens are reserved for structured outputs (they should be inert for most prompts), but we can provide a compatibility build that maps them to existing reserved tokens if that helps.
- Regarding RoPE: our variant is mathematically equivalent for shorter sequences but has better stability at longer sequence lengths; we can include an alternate kernel that uses standard RoPE if Redwood prefers.
- For quantization: we have pre-quantized checkpoints for our 4-bit mixed-block approach and for an INT8 fallback. We will hand over both builds for your validation.

Attachments: (we uploaded a short test bundle to your Drive link) — the bundle contains a small tokenizer mapping script and a quantization manifest.

Emily Jones
Head of Partnerships, Sylph AI
emily.jones@sylph.ai

Subject: Re: Request: Sylph9B entry exception & rollout questions

Timeline & checklist below — I ran a quick local sweep and sketched the tests we'll need before a gated canary:

Must-have tests (pre-canary):
- Tokenizer roundtrip: ensure encode->decode preserves tokens for our top-100 customer prompts including the two special tokens mapped.
- Streaming boundary test: multi-chunk responses with both special tokens present; ensure no token duplication/loss at chunk edges.
- KV-cache alignment: confirm per-step KV cache keys are identical with alternate RoPE kernel; check for off-by-one cache drift up to 1024 steps.
- Latency baseline: perf harness @50rps on the ded-usr-central instance shape; measure p50/p95 for INT8 and 4-bit builds.
- Regeneration test: run our regression prompt set for 24 hours; flag if regeneration rate >2% relative increase.

Proposed window: Friday night -> Sunday early AM (48–60 hours) on a 4-node dedicated pool (NVIDIA A10x4 equivalence). Marissa — can you confirm we can carve that out? If yes, I'll queue a telemetry dashboard and an automated kill-switch: if p95 latency > baseline*1.3 for 10 minutes OR regen rate > 3% for 15 minutes, we terminate and rollback.

Rollforward/pinning ask: We'll need a short-term version hold (pin) for the canary build so autoscaling/auto-rollforward doesn't swap variants mid-run. Ops can unpin if checks pass. I'll draft the kernel toggle and tokenizer mapping flags as runtime params.

Notes on risk: the biggest risk is subtle tokenization differences affecting sampling for few-shot prompts; that's why I want both mapping and fallback tokenizer builds.

Karthik Iyer
Principal Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
